div.p: The PaymentReconciliation resource provides the details, including amount, of a payment and allocates the payment items being paid or adjusted. It supports payments from insurers or other payors, as well as payments collected directly from patients or by third-party payment collectors on behalf of patients.

Payments need to provide a means to associate the amounts paid against specific Claims, Accounts, Invoices, Encounters, Contracts, and other financial exchanges and adjustments in order to reconcile accounts receivable.
The PaymentReconciliation resource is an "event" resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see Workflow Event.

div.p: The PaymentReconciliation resource serves to correlate a payment amount to one or more receivables, such as adjudicated claim amounts appearing on ClaimResponses, amounts payable on Invoices, or amounts associated with Accounts, Encounters, or Contracts. PaymentReconciliation provides the payment details associated with funds issued by a payor or funds collected directly from, or on behalf of, a patient.
The PaymentNotice resource is used to indicate that a payment has been initiated. The resource is used commonly when tracking of payment occurrences is required for regulatory or business purposes.

The ClaimResponse resource is an insurer's adjudication and/or authorization of a set of healthcare-related goods and services for a patient against the patient's insurance coverages and does not indicate that payment has occurred.

For reporting claim and adjudication details to patients or transferring data to patient centered applications, such as Personal Health Record (PHR) application, the ExplanationOfBenefit should be used instead.

p.b: The eClaim domain includes a number of related resources

tr.td: Provides payment details and allocation information for payments from insurers or other payors, and for payments collected directly from patients or by third-party payment collectors on behalf of patients.

A payor's adjudication and/or authorization response to the suite of services provided in a Claim. Typically the ClaimResponse references the Claim but does not duplicate the clinical or financial information provided in the claim.

This resource combines the information from the Claim and the ClaimResponse, stripping out any provider or payor proprietary information, into a unified information model suitable for use for: patient reporting; transferring information to a Personal Health Record system; and, supporting complete claim and adjudication information exchange with regulatory and analytics organizations and other parts of the provider's organization.
An indication that a payment has been initiated or has been cancelled.
